differences.title: 1. ARCHITECTURE
differences.leftDesc: Kafka uses a broker-centric architecture where brokers store and serve topic partitions directly, making them the central point for data management and replication.
differences.rightDesc: Pulsar employs a tiered architecture with brokers serving stateless compute and BookKeeper for durable, bookkeeper-managed storage, enabling independent scaling of compute and storage.

differences.title: 2. STORAGE
differences.rightTitle: Pulsar utilizes Apache BookKeeper, a distributed write-ahead log (WAL) system, providing strong durability and consistency guarantees for message storage.
differences.leftDesc: Kafka brokers store data locally on their disks, relying on replication across brokers for fault tolerance and availability within the cluster.

differences.title: 3. SCALABILITY
differences.leftDesc: Scaling Kafka requires scaling brokers, which impacts both compute and storage simultaneously, potentially leading to over-provisioning.
differences.rightDesc: Pulsar's decoupled nature allows independent scaling of brokers (compute) and BookKeeper nodes (storage), optimizing resource utilization and cost.

differences.title: 4. TENANCY
differences.leftDesc: Kafka's multi-tenancy is typically achieved through topic-level ACLs and quotas, which can be complex to manage and offer limited isolation.
differences.rightDesc: Pulsar provides built-in multi-tenancy with namespaces and robust isolation, offering granular control over resources and security for different users or applications.

differences.title: 5. MESSAGE RETENTION
differences.leftDesc: Kafka retains messages based on time or size, automatically deleting older log segments once thresholds are met.
differences.rightDesc: Pulsar offers flexible retention policies, including time-based, size-based, or a combination, with intelligent offloading to tiered storage.

differences.title: 6. CLIENT INTERACTION
differences.leftDesc: Kafka clients interact directly with brokers to fetch or publish messages from specific topic partitions.
differences.rightDesc: Pulsar clients use a unified client library that communicates with brokers, abstracting away the underlying storage layer complexities.

differences.title: 7. REPLICATION
differences.leftDesc: Kafka uses leader-follower replication where followers track the leader of a partition and catch up by fetching log entries.
differences.rightDesc: Pulsar uses BookKeeper's ensemble and quorum writes for strong consistency. Data is written to a configurable number of BookKeeper bookies.
